LESSON: OBEDIENCE VALUES

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: question(s) Christian 4.1 Sharing By the end of the Sub strand, the learner shou
Topic 4.2: Obedience values

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Obedience values. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: why they should obey obey parents?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the importance of parents and siblings 2.
2. state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: OBEDIENCE VALUES
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Obedience values helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: OBEDIENCE VALUES
Study Obedience values like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the importance of parents and siblings 2.

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the importance of parents and siblings 2.. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the importance of parents and siblings 2..
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Obedience values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the importance of parents and siblings 2.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: State reasons for telling the truth and always. 2.

What this means
In this part you learn to state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2.. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2..
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Obedience values in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Obedience values is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Obedience values” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the importance of parents and siblings 2.)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Obedience values in your own words. (skill: state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2.)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Obedience values to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the importance of parents and siblings 2..
3. Practise this skill: state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2..
4. Make one local Kenya example of Obedience values from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Obedience values: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Obedience values?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why they should obey obey parents?
2. why they should not steal or other peoples’ items?
3. why they should thank their parents thank your parents?
4. When do you thank 3 lessons gratitude to their parents.  Learners to role play how to thank parents your parents?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Obedience values means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the importance of parents and siblings 2..
5. Be able to: state reasons for telling the truth and always. 2..

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
